summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — SAN.PA +10%, CPG.L +4%, EXPN.L +4%, REL.L +3%, REN.AS +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (STMPA.PA -10%, IFX.DE -10%, ANTO.L -9%, BESI.AS -9%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: STMPA.PA (-10.27%) — No company-specific news found; STMicro fell ~10% as Europe's chip stocks erased Monday's rally in a sector-wide semiconductor selloff, with no earnings or M&A driver. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: STMPA.PA is a Paris-listed large-cap European semiconductor that no strategy covers. The move was a sector-wide gap-down with no catalyst, which is hard for momentum or news filters to flag.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up no Sanofi news dated 2026-11-25, so the +9.72% move is unexplained. A pipeline readout, M&A or guidance news is possible but unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SAN.PA is a CAC 40 large-cap pharma, and no strategy includes Euronext Paris names. A +9.7% one-day move is also rare for a mega-cap, so it was likely a gap-up on an unscheduled event that pre-market signals wouldn't have flagged.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gap-and-volume scanner on large-cap EU names outside strategy universes. Alert, or admit to the news-reactive strategy, when |close-to-close| ≥ 5% and volume ≥ 2× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst. CPG.L normally maps to Compass Group, but its price (~2388p) doesn't match the 35.33 close, and the Nov-25 coverage I found showed shares falling, not rising. Likely a technical or sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: no strategy lists it, and the ticker/price mismatch suggests it is a thinly covered or mis-mapped line. With no news catalyst, a +4.5% drift would not trip a gap-up or news-reactive trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: First verify the CPG.L symbol-to-price mapping in the data feed. Then consider adding uk-eu names with a +4% move on ≥1.5x average volume to a momentum watchlist, rather than widening the full universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-25. Searches turned up only older filings (a US$1bn buyback launched in January 2026, routine own-share notices), so this is likely a technical or sector rebound move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. EXPN.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap data/credit-bureau company, and no strategy's universe includes it. With no catalyst, a +4.33% drift would also likely fail gap-up and volume-spike filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 data/analytics names such as EXPN.L to the momentum-trader universe, with an optional 'large-cap no-news drift' rule that enters at +3% intraday on at least 1.2x 20-day average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. RELX (REL.L, about 3,028p) rose 3.2% with no company-specific news in search, so likely a rebound or sector move in data and analytics and information services.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. RELX is a roughly £55bn FTSE 100 large-cap in information services, which the momentum and news-reactive universes don't appear to include. A +3% move on no catalyst also gives a news-reactive bot nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 large-caps with a daily move of at least +3% on volume of at least 1.5x the 20-day average to the momentum-trader's universe, so non-catalyst rebounds in liquid UK names are screened.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for 2026-11-25. REN.AS appears to be RELX's Euronext Amsterdam line, so +2.97% looks like a rebound in quality-growth and information-services stocks, possibly tied to AI sentiment.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. REN.AS is a large-cap, low-beta, dual-listed (LSE/AMS/NYSE) data and analytics name. With no catalyst, a ~3% drift would also fail gap, volume and RSI momentum filters.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change. If wanted, add dual-listed large caps (REL.L / REN.AS) to the uk-eu momentum universe, and require a relative-volume ≥1.5× filter so non-catalyst drifts like this stay excluded.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 25 Nov 2026. Searches turned up only the ongoing 2026 buyback of up to €500M. The move is likely a rebound in data and legal-information software stocks or a general sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. WKL.AS is an Amsterdam-listed large-cap (about €20B+ market cap) in professional information and software. A +2.86% move with no news is below typical gap or volume-spike triggers, so a momentum or news-reactive bot would not have flagged it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Euronext Amsterdam AEX large-caps such as WKL.AS to the uk-eu momentum universe. Gate entries on a relative-strength rule, for example a sector-relative +2% move on at least 1.2x 20-day average volume, instead of requiring a news trigger.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found; STMicro fell ~10% as Europe's chip stocks erased Monday's rally in a sector-wide semiconductor selloff, with no earnings or M&A driver.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STMPA.PA is a Paris-listed large-cap European semiconductor that no strategy covers. The move was a sector-wide gap-down with no catalyst, which is hard for momentum or news filters to flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU semis (STMPA.PA, ASML, Infineon) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a sector-wide drop (e.g. ≥3 of 5 names down >5% on one day) rather than single-name news.

top_movers.catalyst: No Infineon-specific news. Sector selloff in AI-chip names (Nvidia leadership turmoil, new US AI-chip export rules, rising yields) dragged the stock down about 10% to ~43.6, the DAX's worst performer. Reports date the drop to Nov 24, so the date is not fully confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: IFX.DE is a large-cap German semiconductor that no strategy covers. It was also a sector-contagion gap-down with no company catalyst, which momentum and news-reactive filters would likely skip anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU semis (IFX.DE, STM, ASML) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a ≥8% one-day drop with no company-specific news and a ≥40% drawdown from the 52-week high, with a reduced position size.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst for 25 Nov. Searches found no dated news for that day. The likely cause is a copper-price dip and risk-off selling in miners. The Oct 15 Q3 miss and weak 2027 guidance probably added to it.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ANTO.L is a FTSE 100 copper miner, and no strategy's universe includes it. An 8.6% drop with no clear news also looks like a sector or commodity move. A long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot would not trade it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 miners (ANTO.L, GLEN.L, RIO.L) to a commodity-sensitive universe. Add a copper-price (HG=F) drawdown trigger, such as a daily move below -3%, to flag miner sell-offs. Treat it as a no-op if shorting isn't supported.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found; likely a sector-wide tech/semis selloff, with BESI's usual sensitivity to hybrid-bonding/HBM headlines. Earlier 2026 drops had that cause, but none was dated 25 Nov.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI is a mid/large-cap Dutch semicap equipment name on Euronext Amsterdam, which no strategy covers. A sector-driven drop with no clear catalyst would also fail a news-reactive filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small Euronext semicap basket (BESI.AS, ASML.AS, ASMI.AS) to the mean-reversion universe, with a sector-correlation gate that fires when ≥3 members fall more than 5% on the same day.
